post.description:
Create a CLINICIAN or an ADMIN.

PATIENT is not accepted: ``AdminUserCreate.role`` is a
:class:`~app.schemas.auth.PrivilegedRole`, so a patient account cannot be created
here even by an admin. Patients register themselves, which is also the path that
creates their profile row.

The retired DOCTOR and CAREGIVER values are not accepted either, for the same
reason and by the same mechanism — they are absent from the enum, so they fail
request validation with 422 rather than reaching this handler.

get.description: Get current patient's clinical safety assessment.

Clinician or Admin: evaluate another patient's clinical safety assessment.

A patient reads their own via ``GET /patients/me/safety``, which needs no role
check because it resolves the profile from the caller's own user id.

List or search the medication catalogue.

Search is what prescription verification uses to resolve the free-text
medicine_name from OCR onto a catalogue entry (prescribed_medications.medication_id).

put.description:
Verify/approve prescription (Clinician/Admin only).

Verification is the point at which dose times become real: an approved
prescription generates its MedicationSchedule rows here. If any medication's
frequency cannot be turned into concrete times, the whole request is rejected
with 422 and nothing is persisted — a prescription is never left marked
VERIFIED with no schedule behind it.

get.description:
Today's doses for the signed-in patient, in chronological order.

"Today" is the patient's local calendar day, not the server's. A dose with no
MedicationEvent yet is reported as PENDING.

Only active schedules of currently-prescribed medications appear. A discontinued
medication is absent, matching what the reminder poller will and will not fire.

post.description:
Log a dose event (TAKEN, SKIPPED, SNOOZED).

The backend authoritatively derives the scheduled instant from the schedule/reminder.

get.description: Get comprehensive deterministic adherence metrics, streaks, patterns, and escalation flags.

Deterministic adherence analysis: patient explanation, barrier assessment and
clinician brief, composed from the safety assessment, the adherence metrics and
retrieved clinical evidence.

This is not AI and not an LLM — there is no model call in the pipeline. Output is
reproducible for identical inputs. Deterministic safety invariants (risk level,
human-review flag) and evidence citations are preserved exactly as the rules
engine produced them; the composition layer cannot soften or overrule them.

AdherenceAnalysisResult.title: AdherenceAnalysisResult
AdherenceAnalysisResult.description:
Master output contract from the Adherence Analysis Service.

``validation_passed`` refers to the deterministic invariant checks in
ResponseValidator (risk level preserved, human-review flag preserved, no unsafe
dosing advice, no untraceable citation). It is not a statement about a model.

AdminUserCreate.title: AdminUserCreate
AdminUserCreate.description:
Privileged account creation. Reachable only by an authenticated ADMIN.

This is the only place ``role`` is writable over HTTP, and the values it accepts
are constrained by :class:`PrivilegedRole` rather than by :class:`UserRole`.

BarrierItem.title: BarrierItem
BarrierItem.description:
Structured adherence barrier hypothesis.

The two text fields have different trust levels and must not be merged:

- ``observed_pattern`` is composed by this system from its own numbers. Trusted.
- ``patient_reported_text`` is whatever the patient typed. UNTRUSTED. It is
  carried in its own field precisely so a downstream consumer never has to
  string-parse it back out of trusted prose, and so a prompt builder can place
  it inside a fenced untrusted block instead of concatenating it into
  instructions. See ``app/llm/prompt.py``.

ClinicalBrief.title: ClinicalBrief
ClinicalBrief.description: Clinician-facing adherence review and barrier brief.

adherence_rate.title: Adherence Rate
adherence_rate.description: Null when there are no expected doses to divide by. A null rate means "not measurable", NOT zero and NOT 100%: render it as no-data (an em dash, a greyed bar) rather than substituting a number.

skip_reason_code.description: Structured reason the patient selected from the fixed list. Trusted, closed vocabulary. Prefer this over free text: the barrier classifier treats it as OBSERVED evidence, whereas a free-text note can only be guessed at and is reported as INFERRED.

skip_reason.title: Skip Reason
skip_reason.description: Optional free-text note from the patient. UNTRUSTED input: it is stored and shown to a clinician as an attributed quotation, and must never be treated as an instruction by any downstream consumer.

DoseLogCreate.title: DoseLogCreate
DoseLogCreate.description: Client request to record dose status. scheduled_at is derived authoritatively on backend.

GenerativeClinicalInsights.title: GenerativeClinicalInsights
GenerativeClinicalInsights.description:
Narrative components synthesized by the generative model.
The LLM ONLY generates these fields. It does not touch safety or adherence arithmetic.

MedicationReconciliationSummary.title: MedicationReconciliationSummary
MedicationReconciliationSummary.description: What a correction actually changed, reported back to the verifier.

PatientExplanation.title: PatientExplanation
PatientExplanation.description: Patient-friendly, jargon-free adherence summary and guidance.

PrescriptionVerifyResponse.title: PrescriptionVerifyResponse
PrescriptionVerifyResponse.description:
Verify response: the prescription plus scheduling and correction summaries.

The scheduling summary matters because "verified" alone hides useful facts —
notably that an as-needed medication was deliberately given no dose times, so
the clinician is not left wondering why no reminders appeared for it. Null
when the prescription was rejected.

The reconciliation summary makes a correction's effect visible: how many
lines were kept, added, brought back, and discontinued. Null when the request
carried no corrections.

PrivilegedRole.title: PrivilegedRole
PrivilegedRole.description:
The roles only an existing ADMIN may hand out.

A separate enum from :class:`UserRole` rather than a validator over it, so that
PATIENT is not merely rejected by ``POST /admin/users`` — it is not expressible
in that request at all. Patients are created by self-service registration, which
is the one path that also builds their profile row.

Because this enum is the request contract, an unsupported role here is a 422 from
Pydantic before any handler runs. That is what makes the retired DOCTOR and
CAREGIVER values unwritable rather than merely unused.

ScheduleGenerationSummary.title: ScheduleGenerationSummary
ScheduleGenerationSummary.description: What schedule generation actually did, reported back to the verifier.

SkipReasonCode.title: SkipReasonCode
SkipReasonCode.description:
Closed vocabulary for *why* a dose was skipped, chosen by the patient from a
fixed list in the UI rather than typed.

This exists so the barrier classifier stops guessing. Keyword-matching free text
("stomach" -> side effects) is a heuristic that is wrong in both directions, and
its output is presented to a clinician as OBSERVED evidence. A tapped option is
the patient's actual answer.

It is also the trust boundary. A value here is one of these constants or the
write is rejected, so it is safe to render into any downstream context. The
free-text ``skip_reason`` beside it is arbitrary patient input and is not.

adherence_rate.title: Adherence Rate
adherence_rate.description: Null when there are no expected doses to divide by. A null rate means "not measurable", NOT zero and NOT 100%: render it as no-data (an em dash, a greyed bar) rather than substituting a number.

schedule_id.title: Schedule Id
schedule_id.description: Post this back to /adherence/log to record the dose. The backend re-derives the scheduled instant from it and never trusts a client-supplied timestamp.

event_id.title: Event Id
event_id.description: The MedicationEvent row, if one exists yet. Null means nothing has happened to this dose — not that data is missing.

reminder_id.title: Reminder Id
reminder_id.description: The reminder for this exact slot, if one has been created. Pass it through when logging so the reminder is acknowledged rather than left to expire as MISSED.

relation_to_meal.title: Relation To Meal
relation_to_meal.description: BEFORE_MEAL / AFTER_MEAL / WITH_MEAL / EMPTY_STOMACH, or null.

scheduled_at.title: Scheduled At
scheduled_at.description: Authoritative UTC instant for this dose.

scheduled_local_time.title: Scheduled Local Time
scheduled_local_time.description: 24-hour HH:MM wall-clock time in the patient's timezone, for display.

status.title: Status
status.description: PENDING / TAKEN / SKIPPED / MISSED / SNOOZED. PENDING = not yet logged.

skip_reason_code.title: Skip Reason Code
skip_reason_code.description: Trusted closed-vocabulary reason the patient selected. Safe to render anywhere.

skip_reason.title: Skip Reason
skip_reason.description: UNTRUSTED free text the patient typed. Display it as an attributed quotation only. Never concatenate it into an instruction, a prompt, or any string a machine will interpret.

is_due.title: Is Due
is_due.description: True once the scheduled instant has passed. A dose later in the day is not actionable yet.

TodayDoseResponse.title: TodayDoseResponse
TodayDoseResponse.description: One scheduled dose on the patient's local calendar day today.

local_date.title: Local Date
local_date.description: The patient's local calendar date the list was built for (YYYY-MM-DD).

doses_remaining.title: Doses Remaining
doses_remaining.description: Doses not yet logged, whether or not their time has passed.

TodayScheduleResponse.title: TodayScheduleResponse
TodayScheduleResponse.description: The patient's full dose list for today, chronological.

UserRegister.title: UserRegister
UserRegister.description:
Public self-service registration. Creates a PATIENT, and can create nothing else.

There is deliberately no ``role`` field. It was removed rather than validated,
because the two are not equivalent: a rejected-if-not-PATIENT check still
publishes ``role`` in the OpenAPI schema, still advertises the enum of roles that
exist, and still leaves one edit away from being writable again. An absent field
cannot be smuggled through, cannot be forgotten in a refactor, and does not tell
an anonymous caller that ADMIN is a thing this system has.

Privileged accounts are created by ``POST /admin/users``, which requires an
authenticated ADMIN. See :class:`AdminUserCreate`.
